object_description: randomly arranged polygonal buildings defining linked outdoor spaces
design_condition: The buildings use their facades to define a sequence of linked public outdoor spaces, retain the historic movement axis, and orient the school and gym entrances toward the central square.

positive.statement: The careful coordination between built space and the spaces between buildings gives the seemingly random volumes a clear justification.
The precise facades define high-quality public spaces that are coherently linked.
The outdoor-space concept reflects the scale of the existing buildings and retains the historic railway axis as a cycle and footpath.
The sports hall and adjoining rooms are organized coherently and economically.
The exits from the underground car park are ideally organized toward the town hall.
The proposal carefully balances the urban planning and the external spaces.

negative.statement: The escape-route issue still requires the necessary attention.
The balanced outdoor-space qualities continue inside the schoolhouse only to a limited extent.
The classroom floors have minimal daylight in the tightly cut, star-shaped central area.
Access areas and intermediate spaces lack the spatial quality needed to create a flexible learning environment.
The architectural appearance and questions of innovation remain vague.
The large transparent facade areas weaken the economic efficiency of the project.
The high proportion of windows and large volumes below terrain suggest that energy and sustainability were not sufficiently prioritized.
The learning environment has too little spatial potential and is too segmented.
